claim_verdicts.evidence: git-log SYNOPSIS 'git log [<options>] [<revision-range>] [[--] <path>...]'; '[--] <path>...' shows only commits affecting the paths, '--' separates paths from options/revisions. Playground main is linear; lab run lists 3 commits touching total.sh.
git-log: '--oneline' is shorthand for '--pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit'; DESCRIPTION: commits shown in reverse chronological order by default. Lab run prints c812dbd, b3472f6, d915e63 newest first.

git-blame: 'Annotates each line in the given file with information from the revision which last modified the line.' THE DEFAULT FORMAT: 'abbreviated object name for the commit the line came from; author ident (by default the author name and date...); and line number before the line contents.' Lab output matches.

git-blame: 'The origin of lines is automatically followed across whole-file renames... To follow lines moved from one file to another... see the -C and -M options.' '-w Ignore whitespace when comparing the parent's version and the child's' (so without -w whitespace-only changes are attributed).

git-reset: 'set the current branch head (HEAD) to <commit>, optionally modifying index and working tree'; '--soft Does not touch the index file or the working tree at all'; '--mixed Resets the index but not the working tree... This is the default action.'; '--hard Resets the index and working tree. Any changes to tracked files... are discarded. Any untracked files or directories in the way of writing any tracked files are simply deleted.'

git-revert: 'revert the changes that the related patches introduce, and record some new commits that record them.' Note: 'used to record some new commits to reverse the effect of some earlier commits'. Lab run: revert-demo log -3 = e415afb, 57a2d53, c812dbd; b3472f6 still an ancestor.

git-revert '--no-edit With this option, git revert will not start the commit message editor.' git-switch '-c <new-branch> Create a new branch named <new-branch> starting at <start-point> before switching to the branch.' '-q, --quiet Quiet, suppress feedback messages.'

git-reflog: 'record when the tips of branches and other references were updated in the local repository'; 'the HEAD reflog records branch switching'; 'HEAD@{2} means where HEAD used to be two moves ago'. gitrevisions: '<refname>@{<n>}... the n-th prior value of that ref'. git-gc: reflogExpire 90 days, reflogExpireUnreachable 30 days. Lab: reflog-demo's own log has no checkout entries.
git-reflog: 'Reference logs, or "reflogs", record when the tips of branches and other references were updated in the local repository.' Lab run: recovery reset uses only reflog-demo@{1}, no fetch.

git-gc keeps 'objects referenced by ... reflogs (which may reference commits in branches that were later amended or rewound)'; gc.reflogExpireUnreachable 'defaults to 30 days', gc.reflogExpire 'defaults to 90 days'; prune grace '2.weeks.ago'. Supports 'weeks to months'.
git-commit '--amend Replace the tip of the current branch by creating a new commit.' git-gc: reflogs 'may reference commits in branches that were later amended or rewound' and keep them.

gitrevisions: '~<n>... the <n>th generation ancestor of the named commit object, following only the first parents.' Host git 2.46.0: on main 'git merge feature/shipping' -> HEAD^1 'Add a README' (main's tip), HEAD^2 'Charge no shipping over two million'.

git-log: '-<number>' limits to first N commits; '--grep=<pattern>' filters by message; placeholders %H commit hash, %h abbreviated hash, %ad author date (respects --date), %s subject, %n newline; --date=short. Lab output '2026-02-05' confirms YYYY-MM-DD. Shell $( ) and >/dev/null behaviour reproduced by run.

git-blame '--abbrev=<n> Instead of using the default 7+1 hexadecimal digits as the abbreviated object name...'. Lab run: blame 'b3472f64', log 'b3472f6'. Host git 2.46.0 run also prints 8 vs 7 characters.

Lab run (scripts/git and git-playground unchanged stage-0..stage-1, checkout 75bf7d2) prints exactly the lesson's output: log c812dbd/b3472f6/d915e63; blame line 9 of 9 'b3472f64'; line 2 (comment) is c812dbd1; revert e415afb on 57a2d53; 'ok'. main = 6 commits.

Lab run prints exactly the lesson's four blocks (57a2d53 -> b3472f6 -> 57a2d53, c812dbd, b3472f6). After run: 'git branch --contains c812dbd' -> main, reflog-demo; 'git reflog reflog-demo' @{2} 57a2d53 'branch: Created from main', @{1} b3472f6 'reset: moving to HEAD~2' (so before the final reset @{1} was 57a2d53).

Lab (git 2.54.0) and host (git 2.46.0) runs both print 'reset: moving to HEAD~2', 'checkout: moving from main to reflog-demo', 'checkout: moving from feature/currency to main', 'commit: Print the total in đồng'; the last two come from build-history.sh before the demo.

git-push: 'Updates one or more branches... in one or more remote repositories from your local repository'; 'The command by default does not allow an update that is not a fast-forward to prevent such loss of history.' Lab: after 'reset --hard HEAD~1' on main, 'git push origin main' rejected, hint 'Note about fast-forwards'.

build-history.sh exports GIT_AUTHOR_/GIT_COMMITTER_ NAME/EMAIL, per-commit dates, and sets repo user.name/email; blame-and-log.sh lines 24-25 pin revert dates. Lab rerun gave identical ids. A direct Windows-host run gives other ids (file mode/CRLF), but the lesson runs the scripts through the lab.

Conditioned on 'already on the server'. git-push: non-fast-forward refused 'to prevent such loss of history'; '--force ... can cause the remote repository to lose commits'. git-revert: 'record some new commits to reverse the effect of some earlier commits'.

git-commit --amend: 'You should understand the implications of rewriting history if you amend a commit that has already been published.' git-rebase: 'Rebasing (or any other form of rewriting) a branch that others have based work on is a bad idea'.
Definitional, reused from foundation.l2.git-mental-model (content-addressed ids); consistent with git-commit --amend 'creating a new commit'.

git-rebase: 'If you want to fold two or more commits into one, replace the command "pick" for the second and subsequent commits with "squash" or "fixup".' 'The previous branch tip, however, is accessible using the reflog of the current branch (i.e. @{1}, see gitrevisions).'

issues.quote: so the rounding line answers with `b3472f64`
issues.text: The diagram just above names the rounding commit b3472f6, and this sentence gives b3472f64. For a moment I think these are two commits. The explanation that they are the same id at two lengths comes only in section 5.
issues.fix: Add a short clause after '`b3472f64`', e.g. '— the same commit as `b3472f6`, printed one character longer'.

issues.quote: in a straight-line history like the playground's, every commit that changed that path
issues.text: The qualifier 'in a straight-line history' makes me ask what happens in a history that is not straight, and the lesson never says. I stop to wonder whether I am missing a case.
issues.fix: Either drop the qualifier, or add half a sentence saying what differs when the history contains merges (e.g. 'with merges in it, the list can skip some').

issues.quote: revert is the safe shape: it adds, while pushing a reset branch would make the shared repository drop commits it already has, so it refuses.
issues.text: Three 'it's in one sentence: the first means revert, the last means the shared repository. I had to re-read to see who refuses.
issues.fix: Replace 'so it refuses' with 'so the shared repository refuses the push'.
